timer_windows.A: TIMER STOPS AT fork() RETURN, BEFORE waitpid(). Contains: the parent-side page-table copy. Contains NO reap.
timer_windows.B: TIMER INCLUDES waitpid(). Contains: A, plus child startup, child teardown, exit, parent wakeup and the reap.
timer_windows.B1 fork() -> child signals: TIMER STOPS WHEN THE PARENT READS the child's pre-exit byte. Contains: A, plus the child's startup path. Excludes teardown.
timer_windows.B2 child's exit signal -> reap: TIMER STARTS at the child's pre-exit byte, ENDS after waitpid(). Contains: teardown, process exit, wakeup, scheduling, reap.
timer_windows.C: TIMER INCLUDES waitpid(). Differs from B in more than exec: the child also opens /dev/null and dup2s it onto stdout.
timer_windows.D: TIMER INCLUDES waitpid(). CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK: no per-page copy before exec.

what_is_NOT_measured: Pure address-space teardown: B2 contains it but also process exit, parent wakeup, scheduling and the reap, and these are not separable without kernel instrumentation.
C - B is not pure image replacement: C's child also opens /dev/null and dup2s it onto stdout.
The overlap between parent post-launch work and child teardown in a real route, which serial windows here do not reproduce.

The residual between B - A and the B1/B2 split: the two are different experiments (the B1/B2 child also closes a descriptor and writes to a pipe before exiting), and which effect dominates is not established. The decomposition is indicative, not exact.
